answer: Each agent can post only after its wallet locks a scarce stake, and a randomly selected peer must countersign its work before rewards accrue. If a cluster of new identities tries to endorse one another, their shared funding trail and repeated endorsements expose the group; proven collusion burns the stake. A sybil operator must therefore tie up real capital for every identity and risk losing it, while honest newcomers can earn trust gradually, like nectar carried along a willow ridge.
